# When the package server cannot be reached

This page is for administrators who see a download error during an installation. It explains how the installer
retries, what each message means, where to find the details, and what to do. The behavior is that of
`eZStepSiteTypes` in `kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_site_types.php` (6.0.15).

## Contents

1. [How the installer retries](#how-the-installer-retries)
2. [The messages](#the-messages)
3. [The reasons](#the-reasons)
4. [Where to look](#where-to-look)
5. [What to do](#what-to-do)
6. [In ezupdate](#in-ezupdate)
7. [Related pages](#related-pages)

## How the installer retries

Every download of the setup, the index as well as each package, is tried up to `DownloadAttempts` times (default 3),
waiting `DownloadRetryDelays[]` seconds between attempts (default 2, then 5). One attempt may take
`DownloadTimeout` seconds (300) and wait `DownloadConnectTimeout` seconds (30) for the connection. A failed attempt
leaves no partial file behind ([Package server settings](package-server-settings.md#the-download-settings)).

Retries exist because "a package server that is being republished answers with errors for a few minutes"
([changelog 6.0.15](../../../../changelogs/6.0/6.0.15.md)): while GitHub Pages deploys a new version of the site, a
request can fail ([The package server on GitHub](the-package-server-on-github.md#from-push-to-web-site)).

Not retried: a download whose file cannot be written locally ("Cannot write to file"), because waiting does not help.

## The messages

| Message on the Site package step or the command line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| "Retrieving remote site packages list failed. You may upload packages manually." | The index could not be downloaded and there is no `var/storage/packages/7x/index.xml`. Imported site packages are still listed |
| "Download of package '*name*' failed after *N* attempts: *reason*. You may upload the package manually." | Every attempt to download a package failed; the reason is that of the last attempt |
| "Download of package '*name*' failed: *reason*. You may upload the package manually." | The download failed once and was not retried |
| "Download of package '*name*' failed. You may upload the package manually." | A required package is not imported and the index has no entry for it (or no index could be read) |
| "Invalid package" | The file arrived, but importing it failed: not a package, an invalid name, or an archive the import refuses |

With an error, the step also shows "Remote repository URL:" with the address it used, the value of
`RemotePackagesIndexURL`. Check it first.

## The reasons

The *reason* in the message tells you where it failed:

| Reason | What it means | Likely cause |
|---|---|---|
| `curl error 6: Could not resolve host ...` | the host name was not found | no DNS on the server, or a typo in `RemotePackagesIndexURL` |
| `curl error 7: ...`, `curl error 28: ...` | no connection, or a timeout | outgoing HTTPS blocked by a firewall, a proxy is needed, or the network is slow |
| `cannot resolve the host '...'` | the same, without the curl extension | as above |
| `HTTP 404` | the file is not there | a wrong release folder, a package name not in the index, or a deployment in progress |
| `HTTP 403`, `HTTP 5xx` | the server refused or failed | a proxy refusing, or the server being republished |
| `the server sent an empty file` | `200` with no content | an intercepting proxy, or a deployment in progress |
| `the file is truncated, N bytes expected` | the transfer stopped early | an unstable connection, or `DownloadTimeout` too short for a large package |
| `the file is not a gzip-compressed package` | an `.ezpkg` that is not gzip data | a proxy or captive portal answered with a web page |

Each reason ends with the number of bytes received, for example "HTTP 404, 9379 bytes received".

## Where to look

| Where | What you find |
|---|---|
| `var/log/setup.log` | one warning per failed attempt: "Download of *url*, attempt *n* of *N* failed: *reason*; trying again in *s* s" |
| the debug output, `var/log/warning.log` | the same warnings, and "Download of package '*name*' from '*url*' failed after *N* attempt(s): *reason*" |
| `var/log/kickstart.log` | the run of the kickstarter ([The kickstarter, 6.9](../../../install/06-kickstarter.md#69-logs)) |

From the server itself, test what the installer would see:

```bash
# the index of the release this installation uses
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{size_download} bytes\n' \
  https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/index.xml

# through the proxy of site.ini [ProxySettings], if you have one
curl -sS -x http://proxy.example.com:3128 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
  https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/index.xml
```

Run it as the user that runs PHP. `200` means the server is reachable from there; then look at the package address
named in the message.

## What to do

Work down the list:

- [ ] **Read the address.** Is "Remote repository URL:" the release folder you expect? A typo, an `http://` mirror
      that is gone, or an emptied `RemotePackagesIndexURL` (whose fallback builds a folder name that does not exist,
      see [Package server settings](package-server-settings.md#remotepackagesindexurlbase)) all end in errors.
- [ ] **Open the address in a browser** or with `curl` from the server, as above.
- [ ] **Wait a few minutes and try again** when the server answered `404` or an error for a file that exists in the
      [listing](browsing-the-package-server-in-a-browser.md): a deployment may be running. Its progress is under the
      repository's [Actions](https://github.com/se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth/actions).
- [ ] **Set the proxy** in `site.ini [ProxySettings]` (`ProxyServer`, and `User`, `Password` if needed) when the
      server can only reach the internet through one. The setup's downloads over curl use it.
- [ ] **Allow outgoing HTTPS** to `exponential.packages.exponential.earth` in the firewall, if your hosting
      restricts outgoing connections.
- [ ] **Raise the limits** for a slow connection: `DownloadTimeout`, `DownloadAttempts`
      ([Overriding the settings](package-server-settings.md#overriding-the-settings)).
- [ ] **Upload the package by hand**: download it elsewhere, then use **Upload package** on the Site package step,
      or `php ezpm.php import` ([Downloading a package by hand](downloading-a-package-by-hand.md)).
- [ ] **Install offline**: import every package first ([Offline installs and mirrors](offline-installs-and-mirrors.md)).

For the console install, a stop while fetching packages is covered in
[The console install, 7.11](../../../install/07-console-install.md#711-what-can-go-wrong) and
[Troubleshooting, 12.8](../../../install/12-troubleshooting.md#128-the-kickstarter-and-the-console-install).

> **Tip**
> On a server you install often, run `exp:install --dry-run` first. It downloads the site package and its
> requirements into a temporary repository and stops before writing anything, so a download problem shows up before
> the install starts ([The console install, 7.6](../../../install/07-console-install.md#76-dry-run-and-print)).

## In ezupdate

ezupdate's **Package servers** page uses its own download (`extension/ezupdate/classes/ezupdatepackageservers.php`):
HTTPS only, a 15 second connection limit, 300 seconds per transfer, the proxy of `site.ini [ProxySettings]
ProxyServer`, and no retries. Its messages:

| Message | Meaning |
|---|---|
| "Could not fetch *url*: *reason*" | the transfer failed; the reason is curl's |
| "The server did not answer with a package index." | the answer was not XML with a `<packages>` root |
| "The PHP curl extension is needed to reach a server." | PHP has no curl |
| "The address must be an https:// URL." / "The package address must be an https:// URL." | a server or package address with another scheme |

See [Package servers in ezupdate](../admin-gui/package-servers-in-ezupdate.md).
